name: CrystalWorkshop
title: A redesigned interface with new pages and fixes
items: A new app layout (app bar, project explorer, status footer, command palette Ctrl+K, document tabs, icon rail)
A script outline and problems drawer with token-based highlighting
A scene placement outline and viewport toolbar with an inspector showing original and current values
A multi-track cutscene timeline with transport controls and export
XIII motion clips checked with the game's own evaluation beside the preview
An effects layout with a playback timeline and typed fields
A UI Layouts page that edits and previews menu layouts for all three games
A Fonts page for the game's menu fonts
One undo history for the whole project
A redesigned Settings page with row density (Compact or Comfortable)
An export wizard with a package-details step and grouped warnings
Exports and AI assistants kept inside a workspace folder beside the game executable
Revert one script class or a whole file (asks first and can be undone)
Java script tools capped at 30% of memory
Exports never drop a changed file and merge file lists
XIII scene lights no longer draw black
Undo steps whose files changed since are refused
Multi-byte text no longer cut in half
Shards keep their name and version
Unsaved work protected when you leave or switch sessions
The interface no longer freezes during background work

name: CrystalWorkshop
title: First public release
items: Sheets (WDB) and SQL
Text (ZTR)
Models
VFX
Scenes (LYB)
Scripts, actions, events and sound
Crystarium (XIII).
Export
AI (MCP)

name: PulseDepot
title: Redesigned interface and new pages
items: A new look with an icon rail (new Mods and Review pages, a details drawer for the selected mod and confirmations for danger-zone actions)
A Game setup page (game folder, archive and optional data, Crux host, large memory support and Uninstall all in one place)
Create package is now a wizard (Source, Details and Output steps)
Format tools has a search box
A Crux settings page (choices and filters, and reset any setting to its default)
An Apply result page that shows each stage of Apply (if the Crux settings could not be saved, your edits are kept so you can retry them)
An Activity page (recent reviews, applies and Crux repairs for each game)
Preferences for interface density and scale

A large memory support switch for the game executable (on by default; not available where Steam's DRM would reject a changed game file, so on Linux the Proton launch option PROTON_FORCE_LARGE_ADDRESS_AWARE=1 is suggested instead; a change made there by an earlier PulseDepot is undone)
Each mod is checked against the bundled Crux before Apply (and against the raised script capacity setting when it needs it)
Repair Crux installs PulseDepot's Crux into the game folder again (your mods and saves stay as they are)
PulseDepot keeps its own settings in pulsedepot.json next to the program (game folders, launch options and install choices)
The Crux console window is hidden by default
The Mod Settings menu (Configuration, Mod Settings) is now part of Crux and installed with it
Game setup shows the installed and bundled Crux versions and says when an update is available (an older Crux in the game folder is replaced on Apply and the review names it)
Mod lists saved by older versions load again and installed mods are always listed
PulseDepot reports the real state of the game executable if writing the large memory flag fails
Packages are still not code-signed (Windows SmartScreen asks once) and there is no installer

name: PulseDepot
title: First public release
items: Crux in two builds with NovaFix detection
.cws shards
Nova Chrysalia package import
Review/apply
Changelogs and version prompts
Windows and Linux builds

name: Crux
title: Crux 0.2.0-beta
items: The in-game Mod Settings menu (Configuration → Mod Settings) is now built into Crux for FINAL FANTASY XIII, FINAL FANTASY XIII-2 (Steam and Microsoft Store) and LIGHTNING RETURNS: FINAL FANTASY XIII. It lists every installed mod's options in the language the game is running in. It replaces the separate Mod Settings package; PulseDepot turns the old package off.
Support for one more FINAL FANTASY XIII executable.
More room for game scripts in FINAL FANTASY XIII: up to 1024 script classes and 1024 resident battle scripts. Mods that need the extra room require this version of Crux or later.

Startup diagnostics: Crux writes a diagnostics log next to the game's add-ons that you can attach to bug reports. It records which game files and mods Crux finds, and whether the game asks Crux for mod files in the first minutes of play.
The game is still recognised after its executable has been patched to use more memory (Large Address Aware).
Help lines in Mod Settings show only the selected row's own description.
Mod Settings and the game-language detection could fail to start.

name: Accessorize
title: First release
items: Up to seven accessory slots per character, with three new Crystarium accessory nodes per character.
Set for each save slot; off until you turn it on.
Saves only ever hold values the unmodded game accepts.

name: XIII-2 — Accessorize
title: First release
items: Seven accessory slots instead of four, with capacity counted over all seven.
Automatic equipping fills up to seven accessories.
An optional accessory capacity bonus.
Saves always stay within the game's own accessory capacity.
Steam and Microsoft Store versions of the game.
Menu texts in all eleven game languages.

name: Crystal Clear
title: First release
items: Sharper menus, icons and text above 1280x720; nothing changes at 1280x720.
Art sharpness and Text sharpness settings.
Text style: Edge ramp or Smooth curve.
Upscale filter: Edge-adaptive (FSR), Contrast-adaptive (CAS) or Bilinear (retail).
Works with texture-replacement packs.
All settings in Configuration, Mod Settings, Crystal Clear, in all eleven game languages.

name: Honey, I Shrunk the HUD
title: First release
items: Shrinks or enlarges the battle and field HUD around the centre of the screen.
HUD size setting, 25 to 200%, 100% by default.
Menus, the pause screen, shops and the Crystarium always stay at their original size.
Works with Strike a Pose.

name: XIII-2 — Honey, I Shrunk the HUD
title: Settings in Mod Settings
items: Renamed from Field and Battle HUD Scale to Honey, I Shrunk the HUD.
Field HUD Scale, Battle HUD Scale and a Reset to 50% entry are listed under Configuration → Mod Settings, with texts in eleven languages.
The mod no longer adds a Configuration page of its own.
HUD scaling no longer turns itself off when another mod changes the Configuration menu.
Fixed: on the Microsoft Store version, opening Configuration could crash the game.

name: XIII-2 — Honey, I Shrunk the HUD
title: First release
items: Field and battle HUD scaling with separate sizes.
Moogle Clock and Feral Link prompt kept in place.
Scaled cinematic-action prompts.
Mod Settings page.

name: XIII — Loot Your Way
title: More games
items: Renamed from Drop Changes to Loot Your Way.
Works on FINAL FANTASY XIII-2 (Steam and Microsoft Store) and LIGHTNING RETURNS: FINAL FANTASY XIII, each as its own download.
Each game shows only the settings that game supports.
The help for item-type settings names the game's item categories.
The Quantities by item type page shows just the item type.

name: XIII — Loot Your Way
title: First release
items: Drop chance modes (Native, Native + bonus, Fixed) and quantities.
Shroud drop override.
CP rate and gil as a share of CP.
Raised item limit.
Treasure-box quantities.
Catalog bonuses.
Results-screen options.
Settings kept for each save slot.

name: LIGHTNING RETURNS — Loot Your Way
title: LIGHTNING RETURNS
items: Renamed from Drop Changes to Loot Your Way.
Works on LIGHTNING RETURNS: FINAL FANTASY XIII.

name: XIII-2 — Loot Your Way
title: FINAL FANTASY XIII-2
items: Renamed from Drop Changes to Loot Your Way.
Works on FINAL FANTASY XIII-2 (Steam and Microsoft Store).

name: No Post-Battle Healing
title: Maintenance release
items: No gameplay change. The switch is under Configuration → Mod Settings → No Post-Battle Healing.

name: No Post-Battle Healing
title: First release
items: HP carries from a victory into the next battle; a knocked-out member starts with 1 HP.
Restorisol shroud at Unicorn Mart restores the whole party.
Setting and carried HP kept for each save slot.

name: XIII — Pain Your Way
title: More games
items: Renamed from Hard Mode to Pain Your Way.
No gameplay changes for FINAL FANTASY XIII.
This release adds the XIII-2 and LIGHTNING RETURNS builds.

name: XIII — Pain Your Way
title: First release
items: Enemy HP, Strength and Magic multipliers.
Minimums based on your party's average, with an outnumber guard.
Boss scaling.
Easy-mode override.
Settings kept for each save slot.

name: LIGHTNING RETURNS — Pain Your Way
title: LIGHTNING RETURNS
items: Works on LIGHTNING RETURNS: FINAL FANTASY XIII. The HP, Strength and Magic multipliers apply on top of the difficulty you picked; the Easy-mode override is not available there.

name: XIII-2 — Pain Your Way
title: FINAL FANTASY XIII-2
items: Works on FINAL FANTASY XIII-2 (Steam and Microsoft Store).

name: Paradigm Tuning
title: Maintenance release
items: No gameplay changes since 0.1.0.

name: Paradigm Tuning
title: First release
items: Normal, Cross or Wide for each paradigm, chosen in the Paradigm Deck and shown on the paradigm name and on the battle paradigm labels.
Normal is the original party AI; Cross and Wide change how companions in the same role pick their targets.
The Paradigm Deck's help line explains each formation's variant, in all eleven game languages.
Choices kept for each save slot outside your save files.

name: Seventh Ark
title: First release
items: Seventh Ark restoration: the Ark's trials and their labels.
Ark Network warps between the Ark, Orphan's Cradle, Eden, Gran Pulse and the Narthex, with a working teleporter ring at the entrance.
A fallen stone guardian statue in the entrance hall with a voiced, subtitled briefing on your first visit, and a way to check your trial progress.
A unique accessory in each trial's reward chest; 5,000 gil in each of the Treasure Trial's spheres; Nemesis awards 75,000 CP and can drop Dark Matter or a Trapezohedron.
Restored Datalog entries.

name: Strike a Pose
title: First release
items: Strike a Pose: an experimental photo mode for FINAL FANTASY XIII, opened from the main menu entry Photo mode (experimental).
Free-fly camera with lens and roll adjustments, a stored camera and a clear view for screenshots.
Move and pose the characters already in the scene.
Works with Honey, I Shrunk the HUD.
